content_units: Here are the key metrics from the 3-month dataset:
Context note: I treated returns as returned units and calculated return rate as `Returns / Units`.
View   What it should show   Why it matters
1. Monthly revenue by region (grouped bar chart)   Revenue for North, South, and West across Jan–Mar   Makes it easy to compare regional performance and spot momentum shifts
2. Return rate by region and month (line chart)   Monthly return % for each region   Surfaces quality or fulfillment issues that raw return counts can hide

3. Revenue vs units by region (scatter plot)   Each month-region point with Units on x-axis and Revenue on y-axis   Shows pricing consistency, productivity, and whether revenue growth is volume-driven
-   Chart 1:   Grouped bar chart with Month on x-axis, Revenue as value, color by Region
-   Chart 2:   Multi-line chart with Month on x-axis, Return Rate % as value, line by Region
-   Chart 3:   Scatter plot with Units on x-axis, Revenue on y-axis, color by Region
-   North:   Revenue   $133,800  , Units   2,600  , Returns   58  , Return rate   2.23%
-   South:   Revenue   $94,200  , Units   1,830  , Returns   88  , Return rate   4.81%
-   West:   Revenue   $118,400  , Units   2,145  , Returns   62  , Return rate   2.89%
Option 1:   North is the strongest region     Highest revenue every month and steady growth from   $42.0k → $47.0k     Best combination of scale and low returns
Option 2:   South needs attention on returns     Lowest revenue and highest return rate in every month   Return rate stays around   4.6%–5.3%
Option 3:   West is solid but volatile in March     Revenue stayed relatively stable, but returns jumped sharply in March   March return rate rose to   3.55%
Option 4:   Revenue per unit is very consistent     All regions are near   $49–$53 per unit  , suggesting pricing is stable   Performance differences are more about volume and returns than price
